episodes.164338: A strong cold front plowed through the Lower Texas Coast the evening of January 9th. A line of showers and thunderstorms developed along the cold front as it marched south and brought several observations meeting Marine Thunderstorm Winds criteria of gale-force gusts to area waters.
episodes.164378: Rain overspread the area on the afternoon and evening of January 9th ahead of an encroaching cold front. This feature coupled with melting snow from a storm days prior led to localized flooding issues in Wayne and Pocahontas Counties.
episodes.164936: Scattered thunderstorms moved offshore of Brevard County, where one storm produced a strong wind gust at Buoy 41009.
episodes.164937: Scattered thunderstorms moved from interior south-central Florida to the Treasure Coast. One storm became severe as it moved into Saint Lucie County, where it produced ping pong to two inch hail that resulted in damage to numerous vehicles.
episodes.165885: A line of strong thunderstorms ahead of a cold front pushed southeastward from land across Apalachee Bay, bringing a couple of measured wind gusts of 34 knots or greater.
episodes.166059: Strong to severe thunderstorms developed ahead of a cold|front Sunday, producing strong winds over the marine area.
episodes.166298: Waterspouts were observed in association with a remnant cumulus cloud line that drifted south from the Lower Florida Keys over Hawk Channel.  The cloud line became enhanced as a cold front approached from the northwest.

events.county: Hawk Channel From West End Of Seven Mile Bridge To Halfmoon Shoal Out To The Reef
events.narrative: Two waterspouts were observed via the Florida Keys NWS webcams about 5 miles southwest of Key West.  The first waterspout was narrow and rope-like with a visible spray ring.  The condensation cloud extended three-quarters of the way from cloud base to the surface.  The second waterspout was wider and more vertical, with the condensation cloud extending only halfway down from cloud base to the surface.  Movement of the waterspouts was toward the west-southwest.

Numerous reports received from the public of ping pong to golf ball sized hail along State Road 70 near the Saint Lucie Fairgrounds. This hail resulted in significant damage to many vehicles in the area, including broken wind shields, windows, and mirrors.
A trained spotter reported quarter-sized hail.
Several reports received from the public show hail up to two inches in diameter fell west of Fort Pierce, near the Saint Lucie Fairgrounds, intersection of State Road 70, Midway Road, and Shinn Road.
The public reported hail between nickel and quarter size near the PGA Village in Saint Lucie West.
